pair: away points scored vs home points scored (game level)
method: Pearson rho on 136 games, seeded bootstrap 4,000 resamples
betting_implication: drives whether the two legs of a same-game total parlay are independent; a positive rho means the product of the marginals understates the joint

pair: team points for vs team points allowed (club level, weeks 1-9)
betting_implication: a negative value means clubs that score more also concede less — i.e. the spread and the total are moved by the same underlying strength, which is what a ratings model exploits

pair: club margin in one game vs its margin in the next (week over week)
method: Pearson rho on 240 consecutive club-game pairs; the unit is a club-game, not an independent observation, so the interval is a lower bound on the true width
betting_implication: this is the skill-vs-luck number for a team: near zero means last week's blowout tells the market almost nothing and a ratings model has to earn its living on season-long aggregates

pair: win-loss record vs Pythagorean expectation (club level)
method: Pearson rho on 32 clubs; Pythagorean exponent 2 (NFL convention)
betting_implication: the residual is luck: the wins a club got that its point margin did not predict. A strategy that backs the positive residual is backing variance, not skill

pair: rest-day differential (home minus away) vs home margin
method: Pearson rho on 120 games from week 2 onward, kickoff dates read from the official game log; the variable is dominated by +/-7-day bye gaps
betting_implication: rest asymmetry is the cheapest situational feature in the catalogue because it needs no data licence: it is a date arithmetic on the published schedule

pair: home-field advantage, in points (non-neutral games only)
method: not a correlation - a measured coefficient. Mean home margin over 129 non-neutral games: 0.50 pts (SD 13.32, SE 1.17, t = 0.42). Neutral-site games excluded because the log flags them.
betting_implication: this is the only situational coefficient this project may currently assert from its own data. Every other one (Munich travel, short week, altitude) stays at zero until measured on a longer history - which is what keeps the model honest and what makes its error rate the number to watch

pair: home covers the spread AND the game goes over (our own lines)
method: phi coefficient (Pearson on two binaries) on 88 games, seeded bootstrap | parlay arithmetic: marginal p(A)=0.398, p(B)=0.523, observed joint 0.182 vs the product 0.208; a ticket priced on the product is off by 14.35%
betting_implication: the two legs a bettor most often parlay together. A positive phi means the book's independent multiplication of the two prices is too generous to the bettor on the joint and the true joint probability is higher than the product

pair: home covers the spread AND the game goes over (archive prices)
method: phi on 88 games with an archive price; the price column is non-official, the result is official | parlay arithmetic: marginal p(A)=0.364, p(B)=0.534, observed joint 0.136 vs the product 0.194; a ticket priced on the product is off by 42.42%
betting_implication: same measurement against the market's line rather than ours — if the two rows disagree, the coupling is an artefact of where our line sits, not of the games
